title: Fix first-pass approval percent rendered 100x too large in both IDE clients
description: Producer packages/moe-daemon/src/util/metrics.ts emits firstPassApprovalPct on a 0..100 scale (Math.round(count/total*100), comment '// 0..100'). Both consumers multiply by 100 again: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/MetricsPanel.kt:213 formats it * 100.0, and moe-vscode/src/providers/MetricsViewProvider.ts:295 does Math.round(pct * 100). A 50% rate shows as 5000%. Fix the consumers (keep the producer's documented 0..100 contract) and pin the contract with fixtures on both sides so the unit cannot drift again. Source: roadmap 2026-09-10 §4 'Small corrections'.
definitionOfDone: MetricsPanel.kt renders firstPassApprovalPct 0/50/100 as 0%/50%/100% (JUnit test in moe-jetbrains covers all three values)
MetricsViewProvider.ts renders the same three values identically
metrics.ts has a vitest case asserting firstPassApprovalPct is 0..100 for a 1-of-2 first-pass fixture
docs/SCHEMA.md (or the metrics section of docs/MCP_SERVER.md) states the 0..100 unit explicitly
./gradlew test and daemon npm test green

implementationPlan.description: JetBrains first (primary IDE). TDD: write the failing test before touching the render code. Add a pure, headless-testable seam to MetricsPanel.kt — a `companion object { internal fun firstPassApprovalText(pct: Double?): String }` — mirroring the existing companion-seam convention proven by CreateTaskDialog.epicSelectionModel + CreateTaskDialogTest (JUnit 4, no Project/Application/Alarm needed). Step order: (1) create moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/MetricsPanelTest.kt asserting firstPassApprovalText(0.0)=="0%", (50.0)=="50%", (100.0)=="100%", and (null)=="—" (em dash, U+2014 — copy the exact glyph from MetricsPanel.kt line 213, do not retype a hyphen); (2) move the CURRENT expression `"%.0f%%".format(it * 100.0)` verbatim into the new companion function and bind line 213 to `firstPassValue.text = firstPassApprovalText(aggregate.firstPassApprovalPct)`; (3) run `./gradlew test` and RECORD the real numeric failures (expected 50%, got 5000%; expected 100%, got 10000%) — this is the epic-rail evidence that the test fails on the old behaviour, and a mere compile failure does not count; (4) delete only the `* 100.0`, leaving `"%.0f%%".format(it)`, and re-run green. Add a one-line comment above the companion function stating the daemon already emits percent units on 0..100 so consumers must not rescale. The null branch IS the missing-value error handling path and must keep returning the em dash unchanged; likewise leave the surrounding requestMetrics error handling (the swallowed-exception pooled-thread block above renderAggregate), locale handling, whole-number formatting, the hasAny empty-state logic, polling and every other KPI untouched. The tested function MUST be the one renderAggregate actually calls — an unused test-only helper is a rejection.

VS Code consumer (trivial one-line fix, allowed in-task by the epic rail). The buggy formatter lives inside the inline webview script string, so the test must execute that emitted script rather than duplicate its math. Create moe-vscode/tests/metrics-view.test.cjs following the existing harness convention in tests/daemon-start.test.cjs (node:test + typescript transpileModule to CommonJS + node:vm, fake `vscode` module via the context require shim; npm test globs tests/*.test.cjs, so add no runner and no dependency). Build a MetricsViewProvider with a fake extensionUri and a fake MoeDaemonClient whose onMetrics/onConnectionChanged return `{ dispose() {} }`, then call the private renderer entry point `provider['getHtml']()` — it takes no arguments and tolerates a missing view (`this._view?.webview.cspSource ?? ''`). Extract the script with a `/<script>([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/` match and THROW if it does not match. Run that script in a fresh vm context per fixture supplying: `acquireVsCodeApi: () => ({ postMessage() {} })`, a `document` with `querySelectorAll: () => []` and `getElementById: id => elements[id] ??= {}`, and a `window` whose addEventListener captures the 'message' handler (throw if no handler registered). Use bare `{}` stub elements so every DOM property the production script writes is absorbed implicitly by ordinary assignment — the test source must not name any DOM markup-injection property, since the repo forbidden-pattern rail greps for it. Drive the fixture by invoking that captured handler with `{ data: { type: 'aggregate', aggregate: { firstPassApprovalPct: N } } }` and assert elements.kpiFirstPass.textContent is exactly '0%', '50%', '100%' for N = 0/50/100, plus '—' for an omitted field, an explicit null, and a non-number — that typeof guard is the script's missing-value error handling and must survive the edit. Run the test BEFORE the fix and record the 5000%/10000% failures, then change line 295 `Math.round(a.firstPassApprovalPct * 100)` to `Math.round(a.firstPassApprovalPct)` and add the same 'daemon emits 0..100' comment. Missing script, missing handler and unexpected requires must all throw loudly rather than silently pass. Call provider.dispose() in a finally so no listener or poll timer leaks. Leave humaniseMs, escapeHtml, the range chips, the per-epic table and the connection-status error handling untouched.

Pin the producer contract so the unit cannot drift back. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/util/metrics.test.ts (vitest, colocated like the other daemon *.test.ts files) importing the real computeMetricsAggregate and computeDashboardAggregate from './metrics.js'. Do NOT append to an existing test file and do NOT import any module that installs a hoisted vi.mock — a hoisted mock in the same file silently swallows appended cases (known repo gotcha). Build minimal deterministic Task fixtures with fixed ISO timestamps, cast through `as unknown as Task` so only the fields metrics.ts reads are required (status, epicId, metrics.rejectCount). Cases, all mutation-resistant exact-value assertions: two DONE tasks with metrics.rejectCount 0 and 1 give firstPassApprovalPct exactly 50 (not 0.5, not 5000) and the value is within 0..100; 0-of-2 gives exactly 0; 2-of-2 gives exactly 100; adding a non-DONE task with a rejectCount does not change the 50 result (it must not enter the approval denominator); computeDashboardAggregate over the same 1-of-2 input also reports exactly 50; and with no DONE tasks the raw aggregate is 0 while the dashboard field is undefined and absent after a JSON.stringify round-trip — that zero-vs-missing split is the producer's deliberate empty-input error handling and is what the IDE em dash depends on. These lock in already-correct behaviour, so they pass at baseline — that is expected; the fail-on-old-behaviour rail is carried by the two consumer tests. Change nothing in metrics.ts.

Documentation DoD. docs/MCP_SERVER.md already carries the unit as an inline comment in the moe.list_metrics response sample (`firstPassApprovalPct,           // 0..100; first-pass = DONE with rejectCount===0`, around line 1957) and documents omission-when-no-DONE-tasks in the GET_METRICS section (around line 2287). Verify both are still present and correct, then strengthen the list_metrics section with one explicit prose sentence stating that firstPassApprovalPct is an integer percentage on the 0..100 scale and that clients must render it as-is without multiplying by 100. Keep it to a sentence or two next to the existing sample; do not restructure the section, do not duplicate the statement into docs/SCHEMA.md (which covers per-task TaskMetrics, not this aggregate), and do not touch any other tool contract or its documented error handling. Quote the exact final wording and file:line in the step note so QA can check the DoD item without hunting.

Verification gate — one fresh consolidated run from the repo root after all edits, exit codes captured. Windows PowerShell: `& .\moe-jetbrains\gradlew.bat -p moe-jetbrains test; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }; npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }; npm --prefix moe-vscode test; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }; npm --prefix moe-vscode run compile; exit $LASTEXITCODE`. POSIX equivalent: `(cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test) && npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test && npm --prefix moe-vscode test && npm --prefix moe-vscode run compile`. That per-command exit-code check is deliberate error handling: PowerShell does not stop on a failed native command, so an unguarded chain would report green after a red suite. The DoD names ./gradlew test and daemon npm test explicitly, so run the FULL suites, not just the new files. Require a positive executed-test count in each suite and confirm the new cases ran rather than being skipped. The JetBrains Gradle cache is shared with other sessions on this box — serialize with them, never delete or clean shared build outputs, and never regenerate daemon assets for this fix. Pass the exact command, exitCode 0 and a useful outputTail into moe.complete_task verification.

Adversarial self-review, then complete. Load the adversarial-self-review skill and read the whole diff as an attacker. Confirm: renderAggregate in MetricsPanel.kt is bound to the tested companion function (not a parallel copy) and the VS Code assertions run the script actually emitted by getHtml; each client now scales the daemon value exactly once (zero rescaling); 0/50/100 render identically in both clients; missing stays visually distinct from zero on both sides; the producer 1-of-2 fixture is exactly 50; no error handling path regressed on either client (missing-value em dash, webview typeof guard, daemon empty-input branch, pooled-thread request failure); no new timer, listener, vm context or file handle leaks; none of the repo's forbidden patterns appear anywhere in the diff (check the global rail list against the new files) and no secrets or absolute machine paths are in the new tests; no mutable shared formatter state. Explicitly reason about null/empty/negative/huge/NaN inputs and state the deliberate decision in the step note: this task restores the documented finite 0..100 contract only — do NOT add clamping, NaN guards or malformed-value policy, that is out of scope. Verify restoring either consumer multiplier still makes the 50/100 assertions fail, and never weaken an expected value to get green. Stay inside Wave 0: no attempt/candidate/receipt work, no other metrics defects. Leave the pre-existing dirty packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts and every peer/daemon-owned .moe path alone — never stage, revert or clean them, just note them. Report every created/modified path in complete_step.modifiedFiles, then moe.complete_task with the verification evidence and an explicit five-item DoD mapping. If review forces a code change, re-run the full step-5 gate before completing.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Fix the consumers, keep the producer: metrics.ts already documents and emits 0..100 and moe.list_metrics is a published contract, so rescaling the producer would break the wire format and other readers. JetBrains uses a pure companion-object seam instead of bootstrapping an IntelliJ Application/Alarm fixture, because MetricsPanel needs a Project and the repo's JUnit 4 tests are headless (CreateTaskDialog already uses exactly this pattern). VS Code executes the emitted inline webview script in a vm with a tiny DOM stub rather than exporting a formatter and injecting Function.prototype.toString into the HTML (rename-fragile under esbuild) or asserting on source text (which passes even when rendering is broken). Inline fixtures per package avoid new shared fixture plumbing. Six steps / six files; the docs step is small because the unit is already documented and only needs an explicit prose sentence.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Verified live in the tree today: packages/moe-daemon/src/util/metrics.ts:18 declares `firstPassApprovalPct: number;   // 0..100` and lines 92-93 compute Math.round((firstPassCount/approvalCount)*100); only DONE tasks increment approvalCount and first-pass is (m.rejectCount ?? 0) === 0. computeDashboardAggregate (line ~194) passes the value through unchanged and sets it undefined when doneCount is 0. moe-jetbrains MetricsPanel.kt:213 is `firstPassValue.text = aggregate.firstPassApprovalPct?.let { "%.0f%%".format(it * 100.0) } ?: "—"` and MetricsAggregate.firstPassApprovalPct is Double? (Models.kt:149). moe-vscode MetricsViewProvider.ts:294-295 is `Math.round(a.firstPassApprovalPct * 100) + '%'` inside the browser script that getHtml() returns; getHtml() is private, takes no args, and only reads `this._view?.webview.cspSource ?? ''`, so a test can call it with no resolved view. Test conventions: JetBrains JUnit 4 headless with companion seams (CreateTaskDialogTest.kt); VS Code `node --test tests/*.test.cjs` with typescript transpileModule + node:vm + a fake vscode require shim (tests/daemon-start.test.cjs is the only existing example); daemon is vitest with colocated *.test.ts and no metrics test exists yet. docs/MCP_SERVER.md:1957 already comments 0..100 in the list_metrics sample; docs/SCHEMA.md only covers per-task TaskMetrics, not the aggregate.
planningNotes.risks: The JetBrains test is only meaningful if renderAggregate binds to the tested companion function — a copy-paste helper would pass while the panel stays broken; verify the binding in review. The em dash at MetricsPanel.kt:213 is U+2014, so copy the glyph rather than retyping it, and watch file encoding. Kotlin's "%.0f" uses the default locale; keep the existing format string unchanged so behaviour does not shift, and be aware a box with a non-Latin-digit default locale could make the assertion flaky. The VS Code emitted script calls acquireVsCodeApi(), querySelectorAll('.range-chip').forEach and window.addEventListener before renderAggregate is reachable — the stub must supply all three or the script throws silently; make a missing script match or missing message handler fail loudly, and use a fresh vm context per fixture so element state does not bleed. The production script writes the per-epic table through a markup-injection DOM property that the repo forbidden-pattern rail greps for; bare `{}` stub elements absorb that assignment without the test source ever naming it, so keep it that way (that rail rejected the first submission of this very plan; the second was rejected for lacking the literal required phrase). The daemon test must not sit in a file with a hoisted vi.mock (known repo gotcha: appended cases get swallowed). Both consumer tests must fail before the fix — a compile-only failure is not evidence. The shared Gradle cache races with other sessions on this box. packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts was already dirty before this task and belongs to another session; leave it and peer .moe records untouched.
